New York Hits $600M Handle Again on NFL Week 4

Published October 13, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

New York's mobile sportsbooks took in $619.4 million in wagers during NFL Week 4, covering the reporting period that ended October 4, according to New York State Gaming Commission figures reported by Covers.com on October 12. It's the second time in four weeks that the state's regulated handle has crossed the $600 million mark for a single week, a pace that arrived notably earlier in the season than last year's comparable stretch.

A record-setting pace for the nation's biggest mobile market

New York has long been the largest legal mobile sports betting market in the country by handle, and this season's NFL volume is running ahead of 2025's. Covers.com's report described the $619.4 million figure as one of the largest single-week handles in the state's regulated betting history, with the eight licensed online operators combining to hold back roughly $49 million from that total, a hold rate in the high single digits. The report noted New York hadn't cleared that kind of weekly hold since mid-August, making the Week 4 period one of the state's stronger revenue weeks of the season so far on top of the elevated handle.

New York taxes mobile sports betting revenue at a flat rate that is among the highest of any state with legal wagering, which means weeks like this one translate directly into a larger-than-usual tax haul for the state, even before accounting for the rest of the NFL season still to come.

Why it matters to bettors

A rising handle doesn't change the odds or promotions available on any individual app, but it's a useful signal of how competitive — and how saturated — the New York market has become heading into the back half of the NFL season. Heavier weekly volume generally means sportsbooks are fighting harder for market share through promotions and odds boosts, particularly in a market like New York where mobile betting has been legal since January 2022 and has had several full NFL seasons to mature. For context on how a single week's handle and hold relate to each other, see our guide to hold percentage vs. vig.
